import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Calculate effect sizes and p-values for all features
    effects = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if feats.types[i] == 'clinical' or feats.types[i] == 'expression':
            # Calculate effect size (difference in means)
            effect_size = feats.x[feats.y==1, i].mean() - feats.x[feats.y==0, i].mean()
            # Calculate Welch's t-statistic
            n1, n2 = np.sum(feats.y==1), np.sum(feats.y==0)
            var1, var2 = feats.x[feats.y==1, i].var(), feats.x[feats.y==0, i].var()
            t_stat = effect_size / np.sqrt(var1/n1 + var2/n2)
            p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.t.cdf(abs(t_stat), df=n1+n2-2))
            effects.append((abs(effect_size), p_val, fid))
    
    # Sort by effect size (descending) and p-value (ascending)
    effects.sort(reverse=True)
    
    # Select top 3 drivers that are not highly correlated
    selected_drivers = []
    used_features = set()
    
    for _, _, fid in effects[:10]:
        if fid in used_features or len(selected_drivers) >= 3:
            continue
            
        # Check correlation with already selected features
        is_correlated = False
        for selected_fid in selected_drivers:
            col_a = feats.column(selected_fid)
            col_b = feats.column(fid)
            corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, col_a], feats.x[:, col_b])[0, 1]
            if abs(corr) > 0.6:
                is_correlated = True
                break
        
        if not is_correlated:
            selected_drivers.append(fid)
            used_features.add(fid)
    
    drivers = tuple(selected_drivers)
    
    # Use only top 5 features as columns
    columns = tuple([fid for _, _, fid in effects[:5]])
    
    # No interaction terms to keep model small
    products = ()
    
    # Simple weighted score using top features
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(columns[:3]):  # Top 3 features
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        # Weight by standardized effect size
        effect = feats.x[feats.y==1, col_idx].mean() - feats.x[feats.y==0, col_idx].mean()
        loadings[fid] = effect
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
